summary: Tyler County, Texas 70-foot steel tower built by the CCC in the 1930s for the Texas Forest Service; off active service, standing, with a radio repeater in its cab.

facts.design: 70-foot steel tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab, cab provided by Emsco Oil Derrick Co., reached by external vertical ladder
facts.status_note: No longer in active service; cab houses a radio repeater

events.note: Register says built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s; exact year not given, so 1930 is a placeholder for the decade

notes_for_editor: Build date is known only as 'the 1930s' (NHLR); events[0] uses 1930 as a placeholder for the decade, and the story says 'in the 1930s'. NHLR and firelookout.org name the agency Texas Forest Service; the Pine Mills entry names Texas A&M Forest Service. The sources do not reconcile these. The Tyler County Heritage Society has a 'Fire Tower' artifact (index dated January 1, 1941); only a preview was readable and it does not name this tower, so it is not used. No access or visit information found, so access is omitted. Brief coordinates differ from firelookout.org by about 0.0003 degrees, immaterial. Brief status and registration year agree with sources. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the Register footnote was removed from the advice sentence; the company name is given as in the Register ('Emsco Oil Derrick Co.'); the Santa Claus wording is now quoted in full and the Register's administrator line is quoted.
